front: What's the difference between flexion and extension?
back: Flexion decreases the angle of a joint; extension increases it (returning toward anatomical position).

front: Which movement points the toes downward, and which pulls them up toward the shin?
back: Plantarflexion points the toes down; dorsiflexion pulls the foot/toes up.

front: What's the difference between abduction and adduction?
back: Abduction moves a body part away from the midline; adduction moves it toward the midline.

front: What's the difference between inversion and eversion of the foot?
back: Inversion turns the sole inward (toward midline); eversion turns the sole outward (away from midline).

front: What's the difference between pronation and supination of the forearm?
back: Pronation turns the palm down/back; supination turns the palm up/forward.
A cone-shaped combination of flexion, abduction, extension, and adduction in sequence, seen at ball-and-socket and condyloid joints.

front: What's the difference between protraction and retraction of the scapula?
back: Protraction slides the scapula forward/away from the spine; retraction pulls it back toward the spine.

front: What movements are available at the elbow, and why so few?
back: Only flexion and extension — it's a hinge joint that moves in one plane.

front: What does 'scapular upward rotation' mean, and when does it happen?
back: The scapula rotates so the glenoid cavity faces upward — this happens as the arm is raised overhead.
